Reference planes

Source: R/layers-plane.R
geom_plane_3d.Rd

Draws planes through the panel box: planes of constant x, y or z, the three-dimensional counterparts of ggplot2::geom_hline() and ggplot2::geom_vline(), and planes of any orientation, such as a fitted regression plane. Each plane is cut to the panel box and drawn as one flat face, so it intersects surfaces and solids exactly.

Usage

geom_plane_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = "identity",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  xintercept,
  yintercept,
  zintercept,
  normal = NULL,
  point = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

xintercept, yintercept, zintercept

Values at which to draw planes of constant x, y or z. Given here, they replace the layer's data and mapping, as in ggplot2::geom_hline().

normal, point

A plane of any orientation: its normal along x, y and z in the units of the transformed position scales, and a point on it in data units, as in clip_plane_3d(). The point does not train the scales; NULL takes the centre of the panel box.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

Without the arguments above, each row of the data gives one plane through the aesthetics xintercept, yintercept or zintercept, or through the point x, y, z with normal nx, ny, nz (in the units of the transformed position scales).

The plane z = a + b x + c y has normal c(-b, -c, 1) and passes through c(0, 0, a).

Aesthetics

xintercept, yintercept, zintercept, x, y, z, nx, ny, nz, fill, alpha, colour (the outline where the plane meets the box), linewidth, linetype.

See also

clip_plane_3d() cuts layers by a plane.

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 30), y = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 30))
d$z <- exp(-(d$x^2 + d$y^2))
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_surface_3d(fill = "grey85")
p + geom_plane_3d(zintercept = 0.5, fill = "steelblue") + coord_3d()
p + geom_plane_3d(xintercept = c(-1, 1), colour = "grey20") + coord_3d()

fit <- stats::lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
b <- stats::coef(fit)
ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, hp, z = mpg)) +
  geom_point_3d() +
  geom_plane_3d(normal = c(-b[["wt"]], -b[["hp"]], 1), point = c(0, 0, b[[1]])) +
  coord_3d()
